structured_output.summary: Secondary eclipse 91±16 ppm exceeds planet maximum 56 ppm; Sector 110 can test it.
reasons: The open question is the secondary eclipse. secondary_depth_ppm 91 +/- 16 (secondary_depth_error_ppm 16) is a 5.7 sigma detection, 2.2 sigma above secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm 56, and is 49% of fit_depth_ppm 185 — the ratio a diluted eclipsing binary gives. It cannot be an undiluted stellar companion on the target: fit_radius_ratio 0.0120 +/- 0.00102 with transit_grazing False and fit_impact_parameter 0.403 +/- 0.2668 is far too small for a star, and gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses is 0.15. So if the secondary is real the signal is a blend, and if it is a systematic the candidate is a planet. The present data cannot tell which: the phase-curve errors are demonstrably underestimated — ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector gives S6 +68 +/- 29 against S32 -166 +/- 25 (about 6 sigma apart), the net ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm -69 +/- 18 has the unphysical sign and ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses is empty — and the phase-0.5 panel of the all-sector figure shows only unbinned scatter at the +/-3000 ppm level with no binned curve.

The blend scenario is not excluded by the pixel or TRICERATOPS checks. gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip lists Gaia DR3 3222832580043050240 at 15" (G 17.8, needs 30%) and Gaia DR3 3222831828423617536 and 3222831828424528512 at 21" (G 17.2 needs 16%; G 17.7 needs 27%) — ordinary eclipsing-binary depths, all within about one TESS pixel of the target. pixel_verdicts_by_sector is on target only in S98 (SNR 6.1); S6 (SNR 2.7, best star Gaia DR3 3222832958000179840) and S32 (SNR 1.5, best star Gaia DR3 3222832202085922432) are too faint, and their difference images (s0006 and s0032 figures) are jitter dipoles with the best-star marker on other sources. The S98 difference image (s0098 figure) does peak on the target pixel with star, red circle and cross coincident, but a single SNR-6 image cannot separate a 15" neighbour. joint_difference_image_snr, joint_best_source and joint_pixel_verdict are empty. nearby_scenarios_excluded True with nfpp_mean 0 and nfpp_standard_deviation 0 means TRICERATOPS removed the neighbour scenarios on the strength of that one pixel verdict, so fpp_mean 0.08973 +/- 0.0023 does not test them.

Two weaker indicators lean towards a blend but are not decisive. The transit is shorter than the target star predicts: fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.55 and stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 1.69, with fit_scaled_semi_major_axis 2.40 +/- 0.353, mildly favour a smaller, denser host as a blend on a faint neighbour would give. depth_ppm_by_sector S6 101 +/- 38 is about 2.2 sigma shallower than S98 202 +/- 24 and S32 190 +/- 29 (sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.0723), matching the lower-than-expected S6 SNR in other_sector_results (SNR 6.3 versus expected 8.6). Against this, cutout_depth_ppm_by_sector_and_aperture shows no aperture-dependent depth in S32 (225 to 229 ppm) or S98 (204 to 227 ppm) and cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value is 0.189, which argues against a blend; the two sides balance.

The candidate is not a drop. It is independently detected in SPOC data: other_sector_results S32 SNR 8.8 (expected 10.0) and S6 SNR 6.3 (expected 8.6); joint_search_snr 11.7 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 7.6, joint_search_detected True, joint_search_period_days 0.634005 matching fit_period_days 0.6340068 +/- 0.00000132. The all-sector figure shows a roughly 200 ppm, roughly 2 h binned dip in the S98 and S32 panels. odd_even_difference_sigma 0.48 (odd_depth_ppm 171, even_depth_ppm 187) rules out an eclipsing binary at twice the period. planet_radius_earth_radii 2.64 +/- 0.24 on stellar_radius_solar_radii 2.01042 is far below the 22.4 Earth-radius stellar limit and is constrained because transit_grazing is False. gaia_ruwe 0.89, gaia_non_single_star 0, gaia_eclipsing_binary False, vsx_binaries empty. exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are empty, and the record states no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-15. triceratops_verdict is likely planet with most_likely_scenario TP on TIC 220073982.

Host-star caution to carry into any eventual submission: gaia_vbroad_km_s 340.76 on stellar_radius_solar_radii 2.01042 implies a rotation period of at most about 0.30 d (2 pi R / v), half the candidate period and near break-up for a star of this size; gaia_rv_amplitude_robust_km_s 46.24, gaia_rv_epoch_scatter_km_s 14.7 and gaia_rv_chisq_pvalue 0.0115 (gaia_rv_variable False, gaia_rv_nb_transits 16) show the Gaia RVs are poor, so the 0.15 solar-mass limit is weak and RV confirmation will be impractical. Either vbroad is spurious or the TIC parameters are off; this does not decide the case but must be flagged.

What decides it: unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star is 110. When Sector 110 is released, re-run the all-sector verification with S110 included and (a) check whether secondary_depth_ppm stays above secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm by more than about 3 sigma with per-sector ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector values that agree — then propose for drop as a blended eclipsing binary — or falls to within the planetary maximum — then propose for submission; and (b) run the joint S98+S110 difference image (joint_difference_image_snr, joint_best_source, joint_pixel_verdict) to test the 15" and 21" neighbours against TIC 220073982. released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification and other_sectors_absent are empty, so nothing already released is waiting.

Disagreement with the mechanical decision (proposed for submission: no rule holds or drops it) and with the first agent entry of 2026-10-16 04:06 in the verification record, which said held does not apply because all released sectors are used; I agree with the later entry of 04:22. The instructions name a sector that TESS observes and has not released as a hold trigger, and Sector 110 bears directly on the only open question. Submitting now would place a CTOI on ExoFOP with a 5.7 sigma secondary eclipse above the planetary limit and the nearest neighbours untested; waiting for one sector costs little. If Sector 110 does not resolve it, submit with the secondary eclipse and the rapid-rotator host flagged for ground-based photometry of the 15" and 21" neighbours.
